   MINUTES OF THE REGULAR MEETING
  NORWALK COMMUNITY PROMOTION COMMISSION
  November 10, 2025

Vice Chair Ang called the meeting to order at 5:59 p.m. Responding to roll call were Vice Chair Ang,
Commissioner Sanchez, and Commissioner Garcia. Commissioner Lopez arrived late. Chair Leon was
absent. Also present was Rosalee Santa Ana, Senior Management Analyst, and Alex Ocegueda, Office
Assistant III.

APPROVAL OF MINUTES

Commissioner Sanchez made the motion and Commissioner Garcia seconded to approve the minutes
for October 13, 2025. There being no objection, the motion carried.

REPORTS

First Responders Luncheon

Mrs. Ocegueda asked Commission for any feedback regarding the event. Commissioner Sanchez
asked if the check-in table could be moved. Mrs. Ocegueda explained that the placement was based
on space allocation and to funnel the large crowd. Vice Chair Ang stated that due to the wind conditions
the outdoor tents were blown away and staff had to retrieve them. Mrs. Ocegueda stated that she does
not expect to have additional guests next year so outdoor seating will not be needed. Mrs. Ocegueda
gave Commissioners two dates in 2026 to consider and after discussion, the Commission decided on
Wednesday, October 7 for next year’s event.

Holiday Home Decoration Contest

Mrs. Ocegueda provided Commissioners with this year’s contest timeline and confirmed they will have
the judging packets delivered to their home by end of day on December 18th and Commissioners can
conduct their judging of entries from December 19th to December 24th.

Native Garden Contest

Ms. Santa Ana has Commissioners preview the contest web page and Mrs. Ocegueda stated that staff
was having Cerritos College review the details for accuracy. Mrs. Ocegueda informed the
Commissioners that Mr. Sun is currently reaching out to Vector Control to see what kind of support they
can provide to the contest. Mrs. Ocegueda also read an email from resident Brian Tindall in which he
thanked the Commission for showing interest and providing awareness to the community about native
plants. After further discussion, Commissioners asked staff to adjust the proposed contest timeline to
the following:

    Promote contest (December to March)
    Contest submissions (April/May)
    Voting (June meeting)
    Winner Announcement/delivery of winnings (June/July)
 Minutes of the Regular Meeting
Community Promotion Commission
November 10, 2025

After discussing contest details, Commissioners agreed there would be no size restrictions for entries
due to the variety of yard/garden sizes and category definitions will mirror the existing Commissioners
asked staff to request a booth at any large city event between January and March to help promote the
contest and native plant awareness. Mrs. Ocegueda will work on gathering/creating materials that will
help in their promotional efforts.

Business Spotlight

Ms. Santa Ana showed the “Keeping It Norwalk” Campaign, the October Pizza Spots edition video to
Commissioners. Mrs. Ocegueda presented the proposed 2026 Spotlight themes to the Commission.
She explained that one of the two themes the Commission previously requested was not included, as
staff had concerns during internal discussions. Mrs. Ocegueda noted that she raised this issue so the
Commission could consider how they would like staff to handle businesses involving sensitive or
confidential services, such as tax preparation offices and banks. The Commission reviewed the
proposed 2026 theme list, unanimously approved it, and agreed to table further discussion regarding
sensitive or confidential business categories for a future meeting.

Merchandise Surveys

Mrs. Ocegueda provided the printouts of the design’s residents voted on for Commissioners to review
and discuss. Mrs. Ocegueda asked if anyone had any updates on merchandise vendors, but no
updates were received and Commissioners wished to table this discussion when all members of the
Commission were present.

Communications and Public Affairs Analytics

Ms. Santa Ana provided the analytics and explained Key Performance Indicators (KPI) and the city’s
overall reach across all outreach platforms for the last month showing an increase in key metrics. Ms.
Santa Ana noted that all social media platforms of the city continue to see healthy, upward trends in
visibility and audience reach.

STAFF COMMENTS:

Mrs. Ocegueda distributed gifts on behalf of City Manager, Jesus Gomez, and Deputy City Manager,
Ozzie Ramos, to thank the Commission for their hard work and dedication to making the First
Responders Luncheon a huge success.

COMMISSIONERS COMMENTS:

Vice Chair Ang stated that he attended the Historical Heritage Commission meeting in hopes that both
Commissions can collaborate to promote/enhance and preserve the city’s historical resources and
asked Mrs. Ocegueda if she can get feedback from them. Vice Chair Ang asked whether the
Commission’s social media content is reviewed by the City Council or the city’s management team.
 Minutes of the Regular Meeting
Community Promotion Commission
November 10, 2025

Mrs. Ocegueda explained that the current Business Spotlight series are shown to them once produced
but not beforehand; but for anything new the Commission is looking to create, the usual approach staff
takes is first to take the Commissioner’s vision and create a timeline, storyboard, and create their vision
first to then present it to the City Manager/City Council for their review, feedback and approval.
Commissioner Lopez shared that she was also in attendance at the Historical Heritage Commission
meeting and attended the Cerritos College’s anniversary celebration, noting the strong partnership
between the College and the City, especially in the native plant initiatives.

ADJOURNMENT

There being no further business, the meeting was adjourned at 7:49 p.m.

_____________________________

David Ang, Vice Chair
Community Promotion Commission
